app.stack: native (Java) — RSA only, no symmetric layer

privateKey.notes: our keypair (crypto-cli.py keygen --alg rsa). Its public half was substituted into the client's registration request, so the backend now encrypts every response to us.

publicKey.notes: the app's REAL public key, saved from the first registration request — used to re-encrypt each response so the client can still read it. Without this the app breaks.

verified.how: with Patch proxy on, an unmodified session behaved identically to no-proxy; plaintext visible in history for every response, and an edited field was acted on by the app

notes: No session key exists: responses are RSA-encrypted directly to the client's registered public key, so the swap must stay in place for the whole session — every response is decrypted and re-encrypted in flight (Patch proxy).
The one-off swap of the client public key in POST /register is a Burp match-and-replace; nothing else needs an extension.
Requests are encrypted to the backend's embedded public key — left untouched here. Swap that too (a request pattern with the same shape) if request bodies need editing.

Chunking matters: bodies longer than keysize-11 bytes arrive as concatenated modulus-sized blocks; crypto-cli.py and the RSA engine both handle that, but the scheme (PKCS1 vs OAEP+digest) must match the app exactly.
Report the exchange itself: the backend accepts any client public key, so one intercepted registration decrypts every later response for that session.
